newsitem.title: THAILAND: Ranariddh movement opposes Ung Huot at ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh movement opposes Ung Huot at ASEAN.

text.p: A new movement formed by ousted Cambodian co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Tuesday urged ASEAN not to let Foreign Minister Ung Huot represent Phnom Penh at the group's annual meeting this week.

The newly formed Union of Cambodian Democrats (UCD) issued a statement in Bangkok urging the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) not to allow Ung Huot to occupy Cambodia's seat as observer.
Ung Huot was named by strongman Hun Sen to replace Ranariddh as First Prime Minister after the prince was ousted by his co-premier in a bloody putsch in Phnom Penh on July 5 and 6.

"Mr Ung Huot cannot represent Cambodia at this week's ASEAN meeting in Malaysia because he only represents Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and has no credentials from First Prime Minister and FUNCINPEC president Norodom Ranariddh whom he has betrayed by endorsing the illegal and bloody coup d'etat," the UCD statement said.

The formation of the UCD was announced by Ranariddh on Saturday in Bangkok. It consists of his party and three others and aims to find a non-violent, diplomatic solution to the political crisis in Cambodia.

"The UCD urges ASEAN not to send any wrong message and provide any encouragement to Mr Hun Sen by receiving his puppet Ung Huot after his arrogant and short-sighted rejection of ASEAN's mediation to find a peaceful resolution to the current crisis in Cambodia," said the statement, signed on behalf of the UCD by Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Burma and Laos will be admitted on Wednesday.
ASEAN decided to defer its induction of Cambodia as a full member due to the political turmoil in the country. It has not yet set a date for Cambodia's admission.
Ung Huot will attend this week's ASEAN meeting in Kuala Lumpur, but a Malaysian official said on Monday it had not been decided yet in what capacity he would participate.
ASEAN efforts to mediate the dispute between the warring Cambodian premiers were scrapped at the weekend after Hun Sen declined the group's offer.

Ranariddh told reporters in Bangkok on Saturday he was willing to compromise in the search for a solution and said he would have agreed to name his successor as first prime minister if Hun Sen agreed to certain pre-conditions.
The plan was scrapped after Hun Sen refused to allow ASEAN involvement.
ASEAN has yet to take a stance on Ung Huot's position and whether it would recognise him as the country's new first prime minister.
